I’ve been struggling for over a year now with these intense thoughts about contamination. I’m constantly worried that if I touch certain things—especially animals or insects, like dogs or bees—I’ll somehow bring toxins or dirt into my home and expose my wife and dog to danger. It’s not just the animals themselves; it’s the idea that they carry something harmful that I could spread. The fear feels irrational, but I can’t shut it down. 

Because of this, I go out of my way to avoid parks, outdoor events, even walking down certain streets where I might see a dog or a bee. If I do encounter one, I get extremely anxious and spend the next hour scrubbing my hands or wiping down my clothes, even if I didn’t actually touch anything. These rituals take time, and my wife is getting frustrated, but I feel like if I don’t do them, something terrible might happen. The avoidance and cleaning aren't because I’m scared *of* the bee or dog—it’s because of what I think it could lead to. The thoughts come first, then the fear, then the need to act.
D012-D016_h024.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D012-D016_h025.question:
I’ve been having these intense fears around using elevators or going through tunnels—places I can’t escape from easily. It’s been going on for over a year now, and it’s really interfering with school. I’m an art student, and my studio is on the fifth floor of a building with no stairs I can realistically use. I can’t even think about going up without my best friend with me. I make her come every time, and if she’s not around, I just skip class. But even with her there, I’m completely frozen the whole time, terrified something terrible will happen—like the elevator will get stuck and I’ll die from lack of air. 

What’s worse are the thoughts that come after. Like, what if I’m somehow responsible for something bad happening to someone else in there? Then I start counting steps or repeating “safe, safe, safe” in my head until I feel a little less anxious. It’s not really the elevator itself—I mean, maybe it is, but the fear really kicks in when I have these intrusive thoughts. It’s the thoughts I’m trying to neutralize. That’s why I keep doing the mental rituals.
D012-D016_h025.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
